case_name: Zippers Karamchari Union v Union of Inida and Others
facts: MS YKK Corporation, Japan, submitted a proposal representation to the Foreign Investment Promotion Board seeking approval to set up integrated plants for manufacturing zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) with hundred per cent own capital investment with no export obligation.

The petitioners claiming to be the members of various trade unions operating in the companies engaged in manufacture of zip fasteners have filed this Writ Petition u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India seeking mandamus to quash the permission granted to YKK for setting up 'INTEGRATED PLANTS' for manufacturing metallic and non-metallic zip fasteners in India.
Zip fasteners and its components were being manufactured in India since 1949. Since 1971, the manufacturing of zip fasteners has been reserved exclusively for the small scale sector.
There are about 150 small scale units in India engaging over 45,000 workers in the manufacturing process of various components for the end product i.e. zip fastener.

Most of these manufacturers fall within the parameters of small scale industry. They have been supplying zip fasteners to the manufacturers of readymade garments, leather garments and allied articles.
issues: Whether the permission granted to YKK for setting up integrated plants for manufacturing zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) is valid and sustainable.
Whether the reservation contained in Section 29-B(2B) read with item 38(3) in the First Schedule of the Act has been violated by the Central Government.
petitioner_arguments: The permission granted to YKK for setting up integrated plants for manufacturing zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) is ultra vires Section 29-B(2B) of the Act.
The reservation contained in Section 29-B(2B) read with item 38(3) in the First Schedule of the Act has been violated by the Central Government.
respondent_arguments: The permission granted to YKK for setting up integrated plants for manufacturing zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) is valid and sustainable.
The reservation contained in Section 29-B(2B) read with item 38(3) in the First Schedule of the Act has not been violated by the Central Government.
court_reasoning: The Legislature's intent is quite clear that zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) were reserved for small scale industry under Section 29-B(2B) read with Entry 38(3) in the Schedule of the Act.
The concept of integrated plant is well known in the business circle to mean that all components needed for the end product are manufactured under one roof.
holding: The permission granted to YKK for setting up integrated plants for manufacturing zip fasteners (metallic and non-metallic) is valid and sustainable.
